definition: Fraction of chromosomes in a population carrying an allele; MAF is the less common allele's frequency.
Amplicon sequence variant: an exact denoised marker-gene sequence, replacing 97% OTUs.
Systematic technical variation associated with processing groups rather than biology.
Indexed binary format for continuous genome signal tracks.
Testing whether two association signals share the same causal variant.
Data where only relative proportions are informative (sequencing counts, microbiome).
Average number of reads covering a base; 30× WGS means each base is covered ~30 times.
Counts per million; transcripts per million; fragments per kilobase per million. Within-sample units, not for count-based DE models.
Smallest set of variants containing the causal variant with a stated probability (e.g. 95%).
Data-dependent / data-independent acquisition in mass spectrometry.
Estimating cell-type proportions or profiles from mixed (bulk or spot) measurements.
Extra-Poisson variability parameter in negative binomial models.
A droplet or well containing two cells, appearing as one hybrid cell.
Genetic variants associated with expression, splicing, protein abundance, chromatin accessibility or methylation.
False discovery rate: expected proportion of false positives among discoveries; controlled by Benjamini–Hochberg.
Statistical identification of causal variants within an associated locus.
Ratio of abundances between conditions on the log2 scale; 1 means doubling.
Coexistence of mutant and wild-type mitochondrial DNA in a cell.
Genes with more variance than expected for their mean; used for feature selection.
Inferring missing values: untyped genotypes from haplotypes, or missing intensities in proteomics.
One of several transcripts from the same gene, differing by splicing, start or end.
Non-random association of alleles at nearby loci.
Total reads or UMIs for a sample or cell; the main normalisation factor.
Mapping quality: Phred-scaled probability that a read's alignment position is wrong.
Using genetic variants as instruments to estimate causal effects of an exposure on an outcome.
Pooling samples (barcodes, hashtags, TMT tags) and separating them computationally.
Contig length such that contigs of this length or longer contain half the assembly.
Nonsense-mediated decay: degradation of mRNAs with premature stop codons.
Adjusting measurements to remove technical differences (depth, loading) so samples are comparable.
Genomic region with enriched signal in ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq or similar.
Q = −10 log10 P(error); Q30 means a 1 in 1,000 error probability.
Percent spliced in: fraction of transcripts including an alternative segment.
Summing single-cell counts per sample and cell type to analyse with bulk methods.
An inferred ordering of cells along a continuous biological process.
Post-translational modification, e.g. phosphorylation, ubiquitination, glycosylation.
Preferential mapping of reads carrying the reference allele, distorting allele-specific analyses.
Known quantities of exogenous molecules added for calibration (ERCC, SIRVs, sequins).
FDR estimation in proteomics by searching against reversed or shuffled sequences.
Tumour mutational burden: somatic mutations per megabase.
Unique molecular identifier: a random barcode on each molecule before amplification, to count molecules not reads.
Variant allele fraction: proportion of reads supporting the alternative allele.
Variant of uncertain significance in clinical classification.
Weighted nearest neighbours: Seurat's per-cell weighting of modalities for joint analysis.
